content: 1. Norethindrone metabolism is influenced by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Lenacapavir may increase the levels of CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose, potentially raising the risk of adverse reactions. Caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Lesinurad (discontinued) reduces the effects of norethindrone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraception alone is unreliable when taking lesinurad; additional nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 3. Letermovir increases norethindrone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 4. Levoketoconazole increases norethindrone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 5. Lopinavir increases norethindrone levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 6. Lorlatinib decreases norethindrone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Monitor the response to estrogens and progestins when CYP3A4 inducers are added or discontinued, and adjust hormone dosages as needed. Use additional or alternative nonhormonal birth control during and after coadministration with CYP3A4 inducers. 7. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases norethindrone levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during coadministration, and nonhormonal methods are advised. Concomitant use may increase menstrual-related adverse effects (e.g., amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, menorrhagia). 8. Norethindrone increases maraviroc levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised due to the potential for increased toxicity. 9. Mavacamten decreases norethindrone levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Mavacamten may reduce systemic exposure to ethinyl estradiol and progestin, leading to contraceptive failure or breakthrough bleeding. Patients should use contraceptive methods unaffected by CYP450 induction (e.g., intrauterine systems) or add nonhormonal contraception during and for four months after the last mavacamten dose. 10. Norethindrone reduces metformin effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 11. Mifepristone increases norethindrone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism and decreases its effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Backup contraception is recommended. 12. Mitotane decreases norethindrone levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during coadministration, and nonhormonal methods are advised. Concomitant use may increase menstrual-related adverse effects. 13. Nafcillin decreases norethindrone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Nonhormonal contraceptives are advised during therapy. 14. Nelfinavir increases norethindrone levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 15. Nemolizumab decreases norethindrone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Nemolizumab suppresses cytokines, potentially increasing CYP enzyme activity. Monitor for decreased systemic levels of narrow therapeutic CYP substrates after initiating nemolizumab. 16. Phenobarbital decreases norethindrone levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during coadministration, and nonhormonal methods are advised. Concomitant use may increase menstrual-related adverse effects. 17. Phenytoin decreases norethindrone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during coadministration, and nonhormonal methods are advised. Concomitant use may increase menstrual-related adverse effects. 18. Primidone decreases norethindrone levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during coadministration, and nonhormonal methods are advised. Concomitant use may increase menstrual-related adverse effects. 19. Ribociclib increases norethindrone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 20. Rifabutin decreases norethindrone levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during coadministration, and nonhormonal methods are advised. Concomitant use may increase menstrual-related adverse effects. 21. Rifampin decreases norethindrone levels by increasing metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during coadministration, and nonhormonal methods are advised. Concomitant use may increase menstrual-related adverse effects. 22. Rifapentine decreases norethindrone levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during coadministration, and nonhormonal methods are advised. Concomitant use may increase menstrual-related adverse effects. 23. Ritonavir increases norethindrone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 24. Rucaparib increases norethindrone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Adjust CYP3A4 substrate dosages if clinically indicated. 25. Rufinamide decreases norethindrone effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rufinamide is a weak CYP3A4 inducer and may decrease exposure to CYP3A4 substrates. 26. Siltuximab may restore CYP450 enzymatic activity by inhibiting IL-6. Caution is advised when coadministered with CYP substrates with a narrow therapeutic index. Close monitoring is recommended. 27. Stiripentol affects norethindrone metabolism as a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates for increased or decreased effects, and adjust dosages as needed. 28. Sugammadex decreases norethindrone effects through receptor binding competition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Sugammadex may bind to progestogen, reducing its exposure. Patients must use additional nonhormonal contraception (e.g., condoms) for seven days after sugammadex administration. 29. Tazemetostat decreases norethindrone levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 30. Tecovirimat decreases norethindrone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer. 31. Tesamorelin decreases norethindrone levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Alternative contraception is advised. 32. Tipranavir increases norethindrone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 33. Topiramate decreases norethindrone levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during coadministration, and nonhormonal methods are advised. Concomitant use may increase menstrual-related adverse effects. 34. Tucatinib increases norethindrone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce CYP3A4 substrate doses per product labeling. Close monitoring is necessary. 35. Voriconazole increases norethindrone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 36. Suicidal ideation, immune system disorders (e.g., anaphylactoid reactions), and skin disorders (e.g., drug eruptions, angioedema, urticaria) have been reported. Uterine leiomyoma degeneration, pregnancy-related complications, and osteoporosis are potential risks. 37. Contraindications include current or past hormone-sensitive malignancies, hepatic impairment, undiagnosed abnormal uterine bleeding, and hypersensitivity to the drug or its components. Discontinue therapy if hypersensitivity reactions occur. 38. Estrogen use may slightly increase the risk of gallbladder disease. Discontinue therapy if signs of gallbladder disease or jaundice occur. Assess risks and benefits for women with a history of cholestatic jaundice. 39. Monitor blood pressure during therapy, as new or worsening hypertension may occur. Discontinue treatment if blood pressure rises significantly. 40. Women may experience changes in menstrual bleeding patterns, potentially delaying pregnancy recognition. Perform pregnancy testing if pregnancy is suspected and discontinue treatment if confirmed. 41. Based on animal studies, early pregnancy loss may occur. Discontinue therapy if pregnancy occurs. Limited human data are insufficient to evaluate risks of major birth defects or adverse outcomes. 42. Relugolix may be present in human milk, as it has been detected in lactating rats. Estrogen and progestin in breast milk may reduce milk production, particularly before breastfeeding is well established.
